### Observed differences

- Before, ten activities appeared in every trace exactly once: A28, A29, A30, A32 and A33 (first group) and A34–A38 (second group). In the later window each of them appears in only about half of the traces — the first group in about 46 in 100 cases (92 of 200) and the second group in about 55 in 100 cases (109 of 200). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008, OCC009, OCC010]

- Before, the two groups always ran together in the same trace, with every first-group activity preceding every second-group activity. In the later window they are mutually exclusive: they co-occur in about 1 in 200 traces, about 45 in 100 traces contain only first-group activities, and about 54 in 100 contain only second-group activities. Within each group the order stays mixed (both orders in similar proportions) in both windows. [REL025, REL033, REL040, REL046, REL051, REL021, REL056]

- A25 and A26 still occur in every trace in both windows, with A25 before the block and the block before A26 wherever they co-occur. Before, A25's observed outgoing transitions went only to the five first-group activities (about 18–24% each); in the later window they spread over all ten block activities (about 7–13% each), so A25 now enters either group directly. [DIR001, REL001, REL006, REL011, REL016]

- First-group activities gained a direct link to A26: A28, A29 and A33 now send about 22–26% of their observed outgoing transitions to A26, which was not among their observed successors before, when their flow instead continued into second-group activities. [DIR002, DIR003, DIR004]

- Relative event positions: A25's mean position moved later, from about 0.55 to about 0.64 of the trace; first-group activities, when they occur, now sit later (mean about 0.63 to about 0.72–0.73) and second-group activities slightly earlier (about 0.76 to about 0.72–0.74), so both groups now occupy the same mid-late region; A26 is nearly unchanged (about 0.84 to about 0.82). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS008, POS012]

- Pairs of a first-group activity followed within five steps by a second-group activity, previously spread over lags 1–5 in roughly 110–130 traces, appear in only 1 later trace; the after-side distributions of these items rest on that single observation. [LAG001, LAG003, LAG009, LAG015]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the ten-activity block A28–A38, previously executed in full in every case (first A28, A29, A30, A32 and A33 in mixed order, then A34–A38 in mixed order, then A26), became conditional: in the later window roughly 45 in 100 cases execute only the first group and then pass directly to A26, roughly 54 in 100 execute only the second group and then A26, and the two groups now behave as alternatives rather than sequential stages, while A25 still opens and A26 still closes every case. [REL025, OCC001, OCC006, DIR001, DIR002, REL011]

This hypothesis is directly and consistently supported across indicator families: participation of all ten activities fell from 100% to about 46–55%; cross-group co-occurrence collapsed from 100% to about 0.5%; A28, A29 and A33 show new direct transitions to A26 and A25 now feeds both groups; the two groups' positions converge. Chance is an unlikely explanation for the evidence as a whole, since 106 items qualified against about 1 expected without change, and every item ranks above about 199 of 200 random re-splits — though the many relation items describe one underlying trace behaviour rather than independent confirmations. The change is one of participation and routing (each group became skippable, with the remaining group connecting straight to A26), not a reordering: within-group order stays mixed and the A25-before-block and block-before-A26 relations are preserved. [OCC001, OCC006, REL025, DIR002, DIR001, POS003, POS008]

An important competing explanation remains: the later window may mix two distinct case populations (for example two process variants running in parallel) rather than a single process with a routing choice, since the before window shows only the full-block behaviour. In addition, the second group's onward connection to A26 is inferred from co-occurrence order because no direction item with a second-group source qualified, and the lag items rest on a single after observation. [REL025, REL016, LAG001]

Let me analyse this evidence carefully.

Setup:
- 200 traces before, 200 traces after.
- Screening: 209 units tested, 106 items qualified, 1.04 expected without change. Control flow family: 209 tested, 106 items, 1.04 expected. So 106 items vs ~1 expected — vastly more than chance. This is a massive count, many times larger than expected. So the screening comparison passes: the number of items cannot be explained by chance.

Now let me understand the behavioural pattern.

OCC items (CF_OCC):
- A28, A29, A30, A32, A33: before participation 1.0 (100% of traces), after 0.46 (46%). Mean occurrences per trace 1.0 → 0.46. Decrease of 0.54. Support: before 200, after 92.
- A34, A35, A36, A37, A38: before participation 1.0, after 0.545 (about 55%). Decrease 0.455. Support before 200, after 109.

So ten activities that were in every trace before now appear in only about half of traces (46% for A28–A33, ~55% for A34–A38). Recurrence support 0 in both windows (each appears once per trace when present).

DIR items:
- DIR001 (source A25): before, outgoing transitions of A25 go to A32 (0.175), A30 (0.24), A28 (0.195), A33 (0.18), A29 (0.21) — five successors, roughly equal shares (~18–24% each). After: ten successors A37 (0.1), A28 (0.105), A38 (0.09), A33 (0.085), A35 (0.115), A36 (0.13), A30 (0.13), A34 (0.105), A32 (0.07), A29 (0.07) — ten successors, each ~7–13%. So after A25, the flow splits over ten activities instead of five; the original five each dropped to about 7–13%, and five new targets (A34–A38) appear at ~9–13% each.

Wait — but A34–A38 were present in 100% of traces before too (OCC006–OCC010 show participation 1.0 before). So they existed before. Hmm, but DIR001 before profile only shows A28, A29, A30, A32, A33 as successors of A25. After, A25 leads to all ten (A28–A38). Interesting.

- DIR002 (source A28): before, A28's outgoing: A29 0.17, A33 0.215, A30 0.24, A32 0.185, A35 0.045, A38 0.06, A34 0.02, A37 0.045, A36 0.02. After: A30 0.13, A33 0.239, A29 0.239, A32 0.13, A26 0.26. So after, A28 leads mostly to A26 (26%), A29 (24%), A33 (24%), A30/A32 (13% each). A26 is a new successor (26% of A28's outgoing transitions after, absent before).

- DIR003 (source A29): before: A35 0.045, A32 0.225, A33 0.165, A34 0.03, A36 0.045, A30 0.215, A38 0.04, A37 0.045, A28 0.19. After: A33 0.12, A32 0.228, A26 0.25, A28 0.228, A30 0.174. Again A26 appears as a new major successor (25%).

- DIR004 (source A33): before: A28 0.24, A37 0.04, A30 0.145, A32 0.18, A29 0.24, A38 0.045, A36 0.035, A35 0.025, A34 0.05. After: A32 0.239, A29 0.207, A30 0.196, A26 0.217, A28 0.141. Again A26 new (~22%).

So consistently, in the later window, A28, A29, A33 (the activities that still occur in ~46% of traces) now have a direct transition to A26 that they didn't have before (or at least not observed before). This suggests a bypass: instead of going through the full chain A25 → {A28..A33} → {A34..A38} → ... → A26, in the later window about half the cases go directly from A28/A29/A33 to A26, skipping the block A28–A38 (or part of it).

POS items:
- POS001 (A25): position mean 0.549 → 0.635. A25 moved later in relative position (or traces got shorter before it... position is normalized by trace length presumably). Support 1.0 both windows.
- POS002 (A26): mean 0.839 → 0.820, small decrease. Support 1.0 both.
- POS003–POS007 (A28, A29, A30, A32, A33): support 1.0 → 0.46; position mean ~0.63 → ~0.72–0.73. So when they occur, they occur later in the trace.
- POS008–POS012 (A34–A38): support 1.0 → 0.545; position mean ~0.76 → ~0.72–0.74. Slightly earlier when they occur.

Hmm, interesting. A25's position moved later (0.549 → 0.635). A26's position roughly stable (~0.82–0.84).

REL items — this is the big block:
- REL001–REL005 (A25 with A28, A29, A30, A32, A33): before co-occurrence 1.0, A25 before B = 1.0. After: co-occurrence 0.46, A_only (A25 without B) 0.54. So in 54% of later traces, A25 occurs without A28/A29/A30/A32/A33 at all; in 46% both occur, still A25 first.
- REL006–REL010 (A25 with A34–A38): before co-occurrence 1.0, A25 first. After: co-occurrence 0.545, A_only 0.455.
- REL011–REL015 (A26 with A28–A33): before co-occurrence 1.0, B_before_A (i.e., A28 before A26) = 1.0. After: co-occurrence 0.46, A_only (A26 without A28) 0.54. So in 54% of later traces A26 occurs without A28 etc.
- REL016–REL020 (A26 with A34–A38): before co-occurrence 1.0, A34 before A26. After: co-occurrence 0.545, A26-only 0.455.
- REL021–REL024, REL030–REL032, REL038, REL039, REL045 (pairs within {A28, A29, A30, A32, A33}): before co-occurrence 1.0 with mixed order (~50/50 both orders). After: co-occurrence 0.46, neither 0.54. So these five activities now co-occur in only 46% of traces; in 54% neither... wait, "neither" means neither activity in the trace? But each of A28–A33 has participation 0.46. Hmm, if both have participation 0.46 and they always co-occur when present, then co-occurrence would be 0.46 and neither 0.54. Indeed after: co-occurrence 0.46, neither 0.54, A_only 0, B_only 0. So A28–A33 always appear together when they appear at all. And when they co-occur, order is mixed (A_before_B ~0.18–0.27, B_before_A ~0.19–0.28 of all traces; conditional on co-occurrence it's ~50/50). Before, they co-occurred always with mixed order too. So the within-group order is unchanged (mixed), but the group now appears in only 46% of traces.

- REL025–REL029, REL033–REL037, REL040–REL044, REL046–REL055 (pairs across {A28,A29,A30,A32,A33} × {A34–A38}): before co-occurrence 1.0, A_before_B = 1.0 (e.g., A28 before A34 always). After: co-occurrence 0.005 (essentially zero!), A_only 0.455, B_only 0.54. So the first group (A28–A33) and the second group (A34–A38) almost never occur in the same trace anymore. Before, every trace had all of them, with group 1 always before group 2. After, in ~45% of traces only group-1 activities appear, in ~54% only group-2 activities appear, and in ~0.5% both.

This is a striking structural change: the two groups became mutually exclusive alternatives.

- REL056–REL065 (pairs within {A34–A38}): before co-occurrence 1.0, mixed order. After: co-occurrence 0.545, neither 0.455, mixed order when co-occurring. So group 2 activities always appear together when they appear (54.5% of traces).

LAG items:
- LAG001–LAG015: pairs across the two groups (e.g., A28→A36, A29→A34, A30→A36, A32→A34, A33→A34...). Before: lag distribution spread over 1–5 steps. After: support before ~109–129, after 1 (!). So these ordered pairs within five steps essentially vanish — only 1 trace in the later window contains such a pair. The after distribution is a single lag value from one trace. These LAG items have very weak after-support (1 observation), so the "after" distribution is not meaningful; the meaningful fact is that the pair (group-1 activity before group-2 activity within 5 steps) nearly disappeared, consistent with REL025–REL055 showing the groups no longer co-occur.

So the overall picture:

Before: Every trace contained A25, then a block of activities A28, A29, A30, A32, A33 (in mixed order among themselves), then A34–A38 (mixed order), then A26 near the end (~0.84 position). A25 → one of {A28,A29,A30,A32,A33} (roughly equal choice), then within-group transitions, then group 2, then A26. All activities participated in 100% of traces.

After: Two behavioural paths:
- In ~46% of traces (92/200): A25 → group 1 (A28–A33, all present together, mixed order) → A26 directly (A28/A29/A33 now have direct transitions to A26, ~22–26% of their outgoing). Group 2 absent.
- In ~54.5% of traces (109/200): A25 → group 2 (A34–A38, all present together, mixed order) → A26. Group 1 absent.
- The two groups are now mutually exclusive (co-occurrence 0.005, i.e., about 1 in 200 traces has both).
- A25 still in 100% of traces, A26 still in 100% of traces. A25's position moved later (0.55 → 0.64), consistent with traces now containing only one of the two blocks (shorter traces, so A25's relative position shifts... actually if the trace is shorter, A25's relative position would move later if the skipped block was after A25. Yes: before, A25 at 0.55 with both blocks after it; after, only one block after it, so A25 relatively later at 0.64. A26's position roughly stable ~0.82.)

Wait, but POS001 shows A25's position increased from 0.549 to 0.635. And A26 stayed ~0.82–0.84. Hmm, if traces got shorter (one block instead of two), then everything before the removed material shifts later in relative terms, and A26 near the end stays roughly at the same relative position. That's consistent.

Also DIR001: A25 now distributes to ten successors instead of five — because depending on the path, A25 leads into group 1 or group 2. Before, A25 led only into group-1 activities (A28, A29, A30, A32, A33). After, A25 leads into all ten (both groups). Hmm wait, actually before A25's successors were only the five group-1 activities. After, A25's successors include all ten group-1 and group-2 activities. So A25 now directly enters either group.

Hmm, wait. Let me re-check: before, did A25 lead to A34–A38? DIR001 before components: A32 0.175, A30 0.24, A28 0.195, A33 0.18, A29 0.21. No A34–A38. After: all ten. So yes, before the flow from A25 entered group 1 only; group 2 followed group 1. After, A25 enters either group 1 or group 2 directly.

And DIR002/003/004: A28, A29, A33 (group-1 activities, when they occur) now lead directly to A26 (~22–26% of their outgoing transitions), which they didn't before. Before, A28 led to A29, A33, A30, A32 (within group) and weakly to A34–A38 (0.02–0.06). After, A28 leads to A30, A33, A29, A32 (within group) and A26 (0.26). So the hypothesis: a block of activities (A28, A29, A30, A32, A33 followed by A34, A35, A36, A37, A38) that was previously always executed in full (group 1 then group 2) has become optional/conditional: in the later window, roughly half the cases execute only group 1 and then go to A26, and the other half execute only group 2 and then go to A26; the two groups became mutually exclusive alternatives. This is a change in participation/optionality — activities became skippable — not a mere shift in path frequencies between fully-observed alternatives. Actually, per the instructions: "A change in how often existing paths are taken requires that every activity and path involved is observed in a substantial share of traces in both windows" — here the exclusive paths (group-1-only, group-2-only) were not observed at all before (co-occurrence was 1.0 before, so group-1-only had 0 share before). So this is "activities became optional / a group is bypassed" — a participation/structural change, which is a valid hypothesis in its own right.

Support level: The screening comparison: 106 items vs 1.04 expected — many times larger, cannot be explained by chance. Then directness: OCC shows participation drop from 100% to ~46%/~55% for ten activities; REL directly shows the mutual exclusivity (co-occurrence 1.0 → 0.005 across groups; A25-only/A26-only rises to ~0.5); DIR shows new direct edges to A26 from group-1 activities and A25 now entering both groups; POS consistent (A25 later, group activities' support drops). Consistent across many indicators describing the same underlying change. This is a supported hypothesis.

Competing explanations: Could this be two different variants sampled at different rates? Before, 100% participation in all ten activities across all 200 traces — so before there was essentially one variant (at least regarding these activities). After, two exclusive groups. Could the after window be a mixture where some traces come from a different process version? The evidence can't rule out that the after window mixes cases from two different process versions (e.g., a gradual rollout) rather than a single process with a choice. Also, we can't tell whether the choice between groups is driven by case attributes. Also LAG after-support is 1 observation, so lag-based claims are weak — I should note that the LAG items rest on a single after observation and mainly echo the REL co-occurrence collapse.

Also note: the "neither" component in REL021 etc. is 0.54 — meaning neither A28 nor A29 present — consistent with group-1 absent in 54% of traces.

- Group 2 (A34–A38): participation 100% → 54.5% (109 of 200).

So both groups now occupy the same middle-late region — consistent with them being alternatives occupying the same slot. And A25 at 0.64 after... hmm, A25 at 0.635 after, group activities at ~0.72. Before A25 at 0.549, group 1 at 0.63. OK.

Order within groups: before mixed (~50/50 both orders), after still mixed. So no change in within-group ordering constraints.

A26 still after group activities when they co-occur (REL011–REL020: B_before_A = co-occurrence where B is A28 etc... wait let me check. REL011: values [A26, A28]. A = A26, B = A28. So the full before pattern: A25 → group 1 (mixed internal order) → group 2 (mixed internal order) → A26. After: A25 → (group 1 XOR group 2, mixed internal order) → A26.

Number of activities: 10 activities went from mandatory to optional (each present in only ~half of traces). This is "became optional" / "a group of activities is bypassed" — the instructions say this is distinct from a shift in path frequencies. The hypothesis: part of the process (the A28–A38 block) is now executed selectively — either the first half (A28–A33) or the second half (A34–A38), rarely both, and the executed half connects directly to A26.

Hmm, is it "skipped"? In group-1-only traces, group 2 is skipped; in group-2-only traces, group 1 is skipped. Main hypothesis: The block A28–A38, previously executed in full in every case (first A28/A29/A30/A32/A33, then A34–A38, then A26), has become conditional: in the later window about half the cases execute only the first group (A28–A33) and then go directly to A26, while the other half execute only the second group (A34–A38) and then A26; the two groups are now mutually exclusive alternatives rather than sequential stages.
